cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: not bad · /ˌnɑt ˈbæd/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a casual reply meaning fairly good or fairly well. How are you? Not bad, thanks.
nice to see you · /ˌnaɪs tə ˈsi ju/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a friendly greeting when seeing someone you already know. Hi, Puck. Nice to see you again.
how about you · /ˌhaʊ əˈbaʊt ju/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
used to ask the other person the same question you have just answered. I am fine. How about you?
used when leaving someone or ending a conversation. Goodbye, Heart. Have a good day.
see you later · /ˌsi ju ˈleɪtɚ/ · fixed expression · Phrase · New
a casual goodbye when you expect to meet again. See you later. We have class at two.
Cover the words. Say three from memory. Make a new sentence with one, then check the example.

cards.title: meet /mit/ and met /mɛt/
sections: Keep the vowel in meet high and front. Open the jaw a little more for met. Both words end in /t/.
Listen. Say it. Record a second attempt after checking one sound.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 007 - Pronunciation & Listening - 01

articulation.label: meet
articulation.alt: meet: /m/ → /i/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: met
articulation.alt: met: /m/ → /ɛ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: A real exchange
sections:
Heart: Hello. I’m Heart. What’s your name?
Puck: I’m Puck.
Heart: Where are you from?
Puck: I’m from the US. And you?
Heart: I’m from Canada. Nice to meet you.
Puck: Nice to meet you, too.
Listen once. Take Heart’s role, then Puck’s role. Change a detail to make the conversation your own.

sections: Heart meets Puck again after class. “Nice to see you,” she says. “How are you?” Puck replies, “Not bad. How about you?” Heart is well too. They have another class at two. Heart says goodbye, and Puck says, “See you later.”
